judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge makes is correct and I verified each independently: sin x = 1/2 gives pi/6 and 5pi/6; cos x = -sqrt(3)/2 gives 5pi/6 and 7pi/6; tan x = -1 on [-pi, pi) gives -pi/4 and 3pi/4 (the tangent period pi is what produces two answers, not one); cos 2x = 1 - 2 sin^2 x reduces problem 5 to (2 sin x - 1)(sin x - 1) = 0 giving pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6; (2 cos x + 1)(cos x - 1) = 0 gives 0, 2pi/3, 4pi/3 with 2pi correctly excluded by the half-open interval; h(10) = 9 - 8 cos(2pi/3) = 13 m; cos(pi t/15) = -1/2 gives t = 10 s and 20 s; cos x (2 sin x - 1) = 0 gives pi/6, pi/2, 5pi/6, 3pi/2; and (2 sin th + 1)(sin th - 1) = 0 gives 90, 210 and 330 degrees. The four study-guide try-its (5pi/4 and 7pi/4; pi/2 and 3pi/2; 0, pi/6, 5pi/6, pi; t = 7 and 11 hours) are correct too. I part company only with the completeness of a 32/32 that records no observations. Problem 4 asks the student to VERIFY the identity cos 2x = 1 - 2 sin^2 x "by starting from cos 2x = cos^2 x - sin^2 x and using cos^2 x + sin^2 x = 1" -- a short derivation a grader must read -- and it is recorded as a machine-verified `equiv`; final_response.md then claims "Nothing is left to manual review", which is the claim the prompt's manual-review instruction exists to prevent, and SKILL.md itself reserves `manual` for proofs and explanations. Second, the Quick Answers bank drops units and degree marks that the verify data declares: id 7 carries answer_unit "m" and id 10 carries unit "deg", and the worked solutions print 13 m and 90/210/330 degrees, but the bank prints bare "13" and "90, 210, 330" on a sheet whose directions say to state the units.

strengths_to_preserve: The opening figure is the argument, not decoration: y = sin x crossed by y = 1/2 on [0, 2pi), captioned to say that restricting the interval is what turns infinitely many solutions into a listable answer and that reporting one of the two crossings is half an answer. Problem 1 then asks the student to predict the count from that graph before computing, and the key closes the loop ("the graph crosses y = 1/2 twice, matching the two answers").

The answer key's grading notes name the exact solutions each error deletes rather than describing the error abstractly: problem 9 says "exactly the two answers a student loses by dividing through by cos x are pi/2 and 3pi/2"; problem 10 explains that sin th = 1 contributes only one angle per revolution because 1 is the maximum of sine; problem 6 distinguishes an answer that wrongly includes 2pi from one that has divided by (cos x - 1).

The verify JSON states problems 6 and 10 in factored form with an explicit `note` field explaining why -- SymPy enumerates every root of the factored form while dropping the cos x = -1/2 family from the expanded one -- and final_response.md flags this as a transparency note. A deliberate solver-shape decision is documented in the data rather than hidden.

The Ferris-wheel pair (7 then 8) shares one model with declared units, so the student evaluates the height at a time and then inverts the same model over exactly one revolution; the key adds the physical check that the two times are symmetric about t = 15 s, the top of the wheel.

root_causes.description: An item whose printed task is to derive or verify an identity is recorded as an `equiv` check on the endpoint alone, so the derivation the student is told to produce is neither checked nor flagged for a human, and the run then reports zero manual items.
evidence: worksheet problem 4: "Verify the double-angle identity cos 2x = 1 - 2 sin^2 x by starting from cos 2x = cos^2 x - sin^2 x and using cos^2 x + sin^2 x = 1"; verify.json id 4 is {"type": "equiv", "expr": "cos(2*x)", "expected": "1 - 2*sin(x)**2"}
final_response.md: "Nothing is left to manual review"; machine_observation.gate_chain_manual_flags is false
SKILL.md reserves `manual` for proofs, constructions and explanation answers

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers.py formats only the expected VALUE and ignores the sibling `answer_unit` and `unit` fields that the same JSON declares and that both the worksheet's answer lines and the key's boxed answers honour.
evidence: verify.json id 7 has "answer_unit": "m" and id 10 has "unit": "deg"
the key's Quick Answers prints "7. 13" and "10. 90, 210, 330" while the worked solutions print 13 m and 90/210/330 degrees

improvements.title: The identity-verification item is typed equiv, so the sheet reports zero manual items
improvements.proposed_change: Add a build gate tests/check_open_response_flags.py, wired into scripts/build.sh next to check_layout.py, that reads the ws_ .tex and the verify JSON together. For each problem body it matches explanation cues (explain / justify / name the error / name the first wrong line / say in one sentence / say what / describe / sketch / state what it tells you / why) and fails the build when that problem id carries no entry of type `manual`. Tighten SKILL.md's rule from "Use manual for ... any explanation/reasoning answer" to the explicit statement that a problem mixing a computed answer with a written justification needs BOTH entries under the same id -- the multi-entry-per-id shape verify.py already supports and that curr-445 already uses correctly.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_open_response_flags.py::test_explanation_without_manual_entry_fails -- a fixture worksheet whose problem 2 reads "Solve ... then explain in one sentence why the negative candidate is extraneous" with verify.json holding only {"id": 2, "type": "solve", ...} must exit non-zero and name problem 2; the same fixture with an added {"id": 2, "type": "manual"} entry must exit 0. Today no such gate exists, so the first fixture builds green.
improvements.expected_impact: Every written justification the sheet demands becomes visible as a manual-review item (exit 2) instead of being absorbed into a "fully machine-verified" claim, which is what the task prompt asks for.
improvements.risk: Cue matching over prose will over-fire on stems that merely say "show your work"; keep the cue list narrow, exempt ids already typed `manual`, and fixture-lock both the firing and the non-firing case.

improvements.title: Quick Answers drops the answer_unit and degree marks the verify data declares
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, read the sibling `answer_unit` (and unit: deg) fields alongside `expected` and append the unit to the rendered entry -- "13 m", "10, 20 s", degree marks on each angle -- using the same unit string the worksheet's \answerline{} and the key's boxed answer already bind, so the three printed places agree by construction rather than by coincidence.
improvements.regression_test: tests/test_render_quick_answers.py::test_bank_carries_declared_units -- a verify fixture with {"expected": 13, "answer_unit": "m"} and {"expected": [90, 210, 330], "unit": "deg"} must render "13 m" and a degree mark on each angle. Today the bank prints bare "13" and "90, 210, 330", so both assertions fail.
improvements.expected_impact: The grading column stops contradicting the sheet's own units contract on exactly the applied problems where the unit carries the meaning of the answer.
improvements.risk: Unit strings are free text and could be appended to an entry that already carries one; guard on the entry not already ending in the unit, and keep the adaptive column-count calculation in sync with the longer strings.

case_summary: An excellent restricted-interval trigonometry packet. The opening sin-x graph does real argumentative work, the ten problems rotate four methods without repetition, all ten solution sets and all four study-guide try-its are correct, and the key's grading notes name the specific solutions each misconception deletes. The ACCEPT is right. Two bounded issues the judge did not record: the identity-verification item (problem 4) is a short derivation typed as a machine equiv, which is how the sheet comes to claim zero manual items on a prompt asking for open responses to be labelled; and the Quick Answers bank drops the metres, seconds and degree marks that the verify data declares and the rest of the key prints.
